title: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2
alt_titles: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2, WITH OR WITHOUT SITUS INVERSUS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene (614566) on chromosome 19q13.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: For p.Leu108Pro, p.Arg136X and p.Val255CysfsX12, all affected individuals carried homozygous mutations while unaffected parents and siblings carried heterozygous changes consistent with recessive inheritance
checks.explanation: The paper reports only homozygous DNAAF3 mutations and no compound heterozygous cases.

checks.claim: The DNAAF3 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51) encodes a 588 amino acid protein
checks.explanation: The paper gives the chromosome 19q13 location directly.

paragraphs.text: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive disorder of motile cilia. It causes chronic infection of the upper and lower respiratory tract, including neonatal respiratory distress, rhinosinusitis, otitis media, and bronchiectasis, together with male infertility. About half of affected individuals have situs inversus (Kartagener syndrome). In CILD2, ultrastructural studies of the ciliary axoneme show that both the outer and inner dynein arms are missing.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive disorder of motile cilia.
checks.evidence_quote: PCD is usually autosomal recessive and is genetically heterogeneous due to a range of ultrastructural ciliary axoneme defects
checks.explanation: The introduction also describes PCD as arising from dysmotility of motile cilia.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia causes chronic infection of the upper and lower respiratory tract.
checks.evidence_quote: Ineffective airway mucociliary clearance usually manifests within the first year of life with recurrent infections, sinusitis, rhinitis and otitis media, causing a chronic respiratory condition, and progressing to permanent lung damage (bronchiectasis)
checks.explanation: Recurrent infections of the upper airway (sinusitis, rhinitis, otitis media) and the lower airway (bronchiectasis) are described.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia features include neonatal respiratory distress.
checks.evidence_quote: All the PCD families reported here presented with classic clinical symptoms that included neonatal respiratory distress
checks.explanation: Neonatal respiratory distress is listed among the presenting symptoms.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia features include rhinosinusitis.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility
checks.explanation: The paper lists chronic sinusitis.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia features include otitis media.
checks.evidence_quote: recurrent infections, sinusitis, rhinitis and otitis media
checks.explanation: Otitis media is named.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia features include bronchiectasis.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility
checks.explanation: The paper lists bronchiectasis.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia features include male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: giving rise to classical PCD associated with defective left-right organ asymmetry and male infertility
checks.explanation: Male infertility is named.

checks.claim: About half of individuals with primary ciliary dyskinesia have situs inversus (Kartagener syndrome).
checks.evidence_quote: Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome).
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: In CILD2, ultrastructural studies of the ciliary axoneme show absence of both outer and inner dynein arms.
checks.evidence_quote: Electron microscopy confirmed an abnormal ultrastructure missing ODAs and IDAs (Fig. 3a).
checks.explanation: Electron microscopy of patients with DNAAF3 mutations showed loss of both outer and inner dynein arms.

paragraphs.text: CILD2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

checks.claim: CILD2 is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition
checks.explanation: The paper describes PCD, including the 19q-linked form it studied, as autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) found linkage of primary ciliary dyskinesia to the distal long arm of chromosome 19 (19q13) in a family study, establishing a PCD locus at this site.

checks.claim: Meeks et al. (2000) found linkage of primary ciliary dyskinesia to the distal long arm of chromosome 19 (19q13) in a family study.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome scan was performed in five Arabic families. Using GENEHUNTER, a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 was obtained on chromosome 19q13.3-qter
checks.explanation: The linkage to distal 19q in a family study is supported. The paper specifies 19q13.3-qter in five Arabic families.

checks.claim: Meeks et al. (2000) established a primary ciliary dyskinesia locus on chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: These data provide significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirm locus heterogeneity.
checks.explanation: The paper establishes a PCD locus on 19q (19q13.3-qter).

paragraphs.text: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is genetically heterogeneous, and many causative genes have been identified.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: These data provide significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirm locus heterogeneity.
checks.explanation: The paper confirms locus heterogeneity.

checks.claim: Many causative genes for primary ciliary dyskinesia have been identified.
checks.evidence_quote: Disease-causing mutations have been identified in thirteen genes
checks.explanation: The paper reports thirteen known causative genes.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) identified biallelic mutations in the DNAAF3 gene (also called C19orf51) in patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia. In these patients, cilia lacked both outer and inner dynein arms. DNAAF3 is a cytoplasmic dynein assembly factor; its Chlamydomonas ortholog is PF22. Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the patients' axonemes lacked dynein arm components. They also showed that knocking down the zebrafish ortholog caused ciliary motility defects typical of PCD, including laterality abnormalities. These results supported a role for DNAAF3 in the cytoplasmic preassembly of axonemal dyneins.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) identified biallelic mutations in the DNAAF3 gene in patients with primary ciliary dyskinesia.
checks.evidence_quote: We detected homozygous mutations in DNAAF3 in two of the three originally linked families (UCL66/67 and UCL89)
checks.explanation: The homozygous mutations found in three families are biallelic.

checks.claim: The DNAAF3 gene is also called C19orf51.
checks.evidence_quote: DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51)
checks.explanation: The alias C19orf51 is stated directly.

checks.claim: Cilia of the primary ciliary dyskinesia patients with biallelic DNAAF3 mutations studied by Mitchison et al. (2012) lacked both outer and inner dynein arms.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we have identified mutations in the DNAAF3 gene in PCD patients with immotile cilia that lack both outer and inner dynein arms.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the Discussion.

checks.claim: DNAAF3 is a cytoplasmic dynein assembly factor.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe DNAAF3/PF22, a new cytoplasmic factor needed for assembly of axonemal inner and outer dynein arms.
checks.explanation: DNAAF3 is described as a cytoplasmic dynein assembly factor.

checks.claim: The Chlamydomonas ortholog of DNAAF3 is PF22.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that DNAAF3 (also known as PF22), a previously uncharacterized protein, is essential for the preassembly of dyneins
checks.explanation: PF22 is identified as the Chlamydomonas ortholog.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that axonemes of patients with DNAAF3 mutations lacked dynein arm components.
checks.evidence_quote: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.
checks.explanation: Several dynein arm components were missing from patient cilia.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) showed that knockdown of the zebrafish ortholog of DNAAF3 caused ciliary motility defects typical of primary ciliary dyskinesia.
checks.evidence_quote: Knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish likewise disrupts dynein arm assembly and ciliary motility, causing primary ciliary dyskinesia phenotypes that include hydrocephalus and laterality malformations.
checks.explanation: Stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) showed that knockdown of the zebrafish ortholog of DNAAF3 caused laterality abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Like PCD patients, the morphant zebrafish embryos displayed perturbed left-right axis patterning, with about half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos exhibiting either reversed or no heart looping
checks.explanation: Laterality defects were seen in the zebrafish knockdowns.

checks.claim: The findings of Mitchison et al. (2012) supported a role for DNAAF3 in the cytoplasmic preassembly of axonemal dyneins.
checks.evidence_quote: These results support the existence of a conserved, multistep pathway for the cytoplasmic formation of assembly competent ciliary dynein complexes.
checks.explanation: The paper concludes that DNAAF3 acts in cytoplasmic dynein preassembly.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Absent outer and inner dynein arms
